**Measured, not published.** The F-15's flight manual, T.O. 1F-15A-1, gives no stall speed: its section VI has the angle of attack settle at 45 units or more at full aft stick, at 100 knots or less, sinking - the lift never breaks. So this is the speed at which the model's lift coefficient is first a maximum in a deceleration of a knot a second, as 14 CFR 25.103(b) defines a stall speed for an aeroplane that has no break. That maximum is where the model's lift table peaks, at 32 degrees of alpha - the table's, from JSBSim's f15, not a published one. It was 151.06 until the pitching moment was made NASA's (tools/make_f15c.py), the speed where the stabilator ran out at 18 degrees. Measured on 2026-10-02 from entry speeds of 160, 200 and 240 knots: 112.13, 112.26 and 112.15. What it asserts is that the model still does what it did, not that the aeroplane does it.

**Measured, not published.** Neither the Standard Aircraft Characteristics nor the flight manual gives a climbing speed, or a rate of climb at this loading and speed. Both are the model's own, taken on 2026-09-23, and the rate measured again, 24,556, on 2026-10-02 with the pitching moment made NASA's. The curve is still flat here, so the speed is not what the ninety-five per cent test picked but the floor under it then: **1.3 times the stall speed measured then, 151.1 knots**. The stall is now measured at 112, whose floor would be 146. **200 is kept by decision, not by that rule**: it is where the take-off and climb lessons were measured, and a climb taught at 146 knots is not one the manual flies. A fighter has so much thrust to spare that it climbs within a few per cent of its best rate over hundreds of knots, and taking the peak would have taught a climb at 522 knots.
published_figures.plan_speeds: The slowest, 160 kt, is its approach speed, the slowest any plan was ever let fly it: flown clean, it held all four ways round its 3,704 m circle. The fastest, 360 kt, a fifth over its start speed, held all four ways.
published_figures.glide_speeds: 170 kt; from 160, the slowest a route may fly it, to 165 it stalled.
